affluent

/AF-loo-uhnt/ - the stress falls on AF · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Affluent means wealthy — supplied with money so plentiful that it seems to flow in on its own.

The tennis club anchors the affluent end of town, where even the birdhouses wear little copper roofs.

Example

The listing agent saved Fairview Court for last. Circular driveways, a koi pond per lawn, three-car garages with nothing parked outside them — an affluent street announces itself quietly, in upkeep rather than in signs. 'You're not buying a house here,' she admitted, 'you're buying the zip code.'

Affluent fits because the street's comfort rests on plainly plentiful money — the word comes from wealth that flows in steadily, more arriving than anyone needs to spend. It describes people, households, and neighborhoods with money to spare, not any one shiny object.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

wealthy: the plain, broad word for having a great deal of money. Affluent says the same thing with a picture inside it — wealth that flows, funding comfort as it comes — and it attaches most naturally to communities, families, and customers.

prosperous: flourishing — succeeding and growing, especially in business or trade. A town can be prosperous because its factories are thriving; affluent skips the trajectory and states the result: the money is already there.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

impoverished: made poor; stripped of money and resources

destitute: lacking even the basics — the far end of poverty

Where it sits · how far the money flows past need

comfortable → affluent → opulent

comfortable vs. affluent: Comfortable is weaker than affluent: a comfortable family covers every bill with a little left over, while an affluent one has money enough to stop thinking about the bills at all.

opulent vs. affluent: Opulent is stronger than affluent: affluent money quietly funds ease, but opulence spills into display — marble, gilt, and chandeliers meant to be seen.

Which word fits?

Answer correctly to continue.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — af-: toward (Latin ad-, reshaped before f)

Root — flu-: to flow (Latin fluere)

Suffix — -ent: doing or being — Latin's -ing

Put it together: Af- (toward) + flu- (to flow) + -ent (in the act of) = 'flowing toward.' The picture is a current of money running in someone's direction — the affluent are those the stream flows to, with more arriving than need can drain.

Use the root in a new word: confluence: The festival began as a confluence of jazz players and quilting circles that nobody had planned.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / formal — journalism, demographics, real estate

Affluent is the reporter's polite word for rich, and it prefers groups and places: affluent suburbs, affluent shoppers, an affluent clientele. It describes the people and communities the money flows to — a single object can be luxurious or overpriced, but not affluent. And keep it off displays: for wealth that performs itself in marble and gilt, the word is opulent.
